answer: At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a ocean tag. The delta cap is enforced at intake and pulse shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, as each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 31 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
